list: Official 55-trophy list, verified against Exophase and PSNProfiles, 20 Nov 2026
sources: Official trophy names, descriptions and grades: Exophase (exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies) and PSNProfiles (psnprofiles.com/trophies/43531-grand-theft-auto-vi), agreeing on all 55
Counts used in guides (14 Top Fun locations, 42 Shooting Range golds, 9 activity types, 8 garage properties): community trackers, cross-checked on Exophase and PSNProfiles
Seven trophies are flagged method-unconfirmed: their names and descriptions are official, but no verified unlock method exists yet in public guides
notes: All guide text is original, written for this guide. Difficulty is a 1-5 rating (1 = automatic, 5 = long grind). Hours are rough estimates for a first-time player. Only Positive Mental Attitude is missable: one meditation spot sits in Chapter 1, so do it before the chapter ends.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the reward for everything else: it pops the moment the other 54 trophies are yours, so there is no separate trick to it. Treat the guide as a whole as the method — finish the story, clear the stranger strands, then sweep the activities, collectibles and robberies. Expect around 200 hours in total; the long tail is A Long Road at 100% completion, not any single hard trophy.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, to the end. It is unmissable story progress and unlocks as the mission completes, so just follow the on-screen objectives and do not worry about optional goals — none of them gate this trophy.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1. Before you move on, stop and do the meditation spot at Jason's house — it is the one spot in the game tied to Positive Mental Attitude that can be left behind when the chapter ends. Keep a separate manual save at the chapter transition so a missed step never costs a full replay.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2. Between story beats, bank the easy open-world progress that is already around you: discover new vehicles for Whip It Good and scan locations for You WAiNKer, since both count passively while you drive between missions.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3. By now the map is opening up, so use the gaps between missions to try one of each activity type — that quietly builds Master of None — and to win a race or two toward Earn Cash, Not Kudos instead of leaving all 20 for the endgame.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4. Before the finale, check your stranger strands: the five side characters (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) each have a final mission with its own trophy, and their strands are easiest to finish while the story is still giving you reasons to cross the map.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Play the final mission to its conclusion. It unlocks on completion regardless of how you approach it, so pick the approach you are comfortable with rather than the flashiest one. Once it pops, the 100% completion checklist opens in the Progress menu — that is where the rest of the platinum lives.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. It arrives as part of the campaign, so it cannot be skipped or locked out — just play through it when it appears in your mission list and the trophy follows on completion.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions tend to run longer than a standard mission, so stock up on armour and ammo beforehand and keep a manual save from just before it starts — a failed attempt then costs minutes, not a replay of the setup.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Like the other mission trophies it is automatic story progress: it unlocks when the mission ends, with no optional objective attached to it.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. Play it when it appears in the campaign flow; there is nothing to prepare in advance and nothing to miss, since the trophy is tied to finishing the mission itself.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown. Expect a heavier combat stretch than the average mission, so go in with full armour and a ranged loadout you trust. The trophy pops on completion either way — the difficulty is in surviving the mission, not in any hidden requirement.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. As with the other mission trophies, finishing the mission is the whole requirement. Save manually before starting so a wipe puts you back at the mission door, not hours earlier.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.source: Official trophy description; completion checklist counts: Exophase / PSNProfiles community reports
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the in-game completion checklist, which opens in the Progress menu after the story ends. It does not demand literally everything: community tracking puts the checklist at story progress plus 100 optional tasks, 200 of 277 vehicles scanned, 100 of 255 animals studied, 70 of 80 challenges, all 42 Shooting Range golds, the required drone races and robberies, and the stunt and exploration totals. Work from the checklist itself, not from memory — it tells you exactly which buckets are short. This is the longest single trophy on the list, so treat it as the endgame and let the other trophies feed into it instead of grinding it in isolation.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, airtime and the like — anywhere in Leonida. Do not grind this in one sitting: stunts accumulate naturally across the whole playthrough, so check your count in the stats menu now and then and only dedicate a session to it in the endgame if you are still short. A fast bike on the highway ramps and the airport jumps is the quickest way to farm the remainder.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.source: Official trophy description; 9 activity types: Exophase / PSNProfiles community reports
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once: racing, fishing, shooting range, arcade games, drone racing, bowling, meditation, hunting and the WAiNK scanning walks. The cheapest way to clear it is a single tour early in the game — one taste of each, no mastery needed — and the trophy pops as soon as the ninth type registers. If it has not popped, the activity menu shows which types you have touched and which you have not.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.source: Official trophy description; 42 challenges: Exophase / PSNProfiles community reports
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the most skill-gated trophy outside 100% completion, so treat it as a practice project: learn one weapon class at a time, use the range's own scoring feedback to find where you bleed points, and take the hardest challenges last when your aim is warm. Gold needs clean runs, not fast ones — slow down, land headshots, and restart a challenge the moment a run goes bad instead of finishing it.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.source: Official trophy description; 14 locations: Exophase / PSNProfiles community reports
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations across Leonida. Learn the racing line before chasing the win: fly the course once slowly to memorise the gates, then race it for real. Knock the locations out region by region while you are already travelling for other trophies, and keep a note of which locations are done — the game does not make the remaining ones obvious.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different events, not the same race 20 times. Mix street races, off-road and water events so you are always ticking a new one off, and use a vehicle tuned for the event type instead of forcing one favourite car into every race. The race menu shows which events you have won, so sweep the ones you have never tried first.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is a timing game, not a gear check: watch the tension and reel in bursts instead of holding the line, and let the fish run when the line strains. Challenge Cal when you find him at a fishing spot, and if you lose, you can try again — there is no penalty for a failed attempt.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Play any arcade game to completion. Pick the shortest cabinet you can find — a quick arcade game takes minutes — and just finish it; there is no score threshold. Do this the first time you pass an arcade so it never becomes a chore you have to travel back for.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Play through Andy's stranger strand to its final mission and complete it. Stranger strands unlock as you explore and progress the story, so if Andy's missions are not appearing, advance the campaign a little and check the map for his marker. Finish the whole strand in one stretch while you are in the area — the final mission is the trophy, and the earlier missions are the key to reaching it.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Play through Kenton's stranger strand to its final mission and complete it. Kenton's strand is water-flavoured, so keep a boat-ready mindset: travel by water when his missions ask for it instead of fighting the map by road. As with the other stranger finals, the trophy is the final mission itself, so the work is simply reaching it.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Play through Billy's stranger strand to its final mission and complete it. Billy's missions lean on riding, so a good bike makes the strand faster and less frustrating. Clear his missions as they appear rather than letting them pile up — five strands left to the endgame is a dull slog, one strand finished now is momentum.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands across Leonida. The five named characters (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) count toward the eight, so you need three more beyond them — explore the map markers and talk to the strangers you find. Track strands in a notebook or in this guide's checklist: a strand only counts when its final mission is done, so half-finished strands are the classic way to stall at 7 of 8.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Play through Randy's stranger strand to its final mission and complete it. Randy's strand is about moving product, so expect driving and delivery legs — a fast, sturdy car beats a flashy one here. Finish the strand when it opens rather than saving it for the cleanup phase.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Play through Tyrone's stranger strand to its final mission and complete it. Tyrone's missions reward steady driving over showboating, so keep your vehicle intact and your wanted level low between stops. One focused session clears the whole strand.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.source: Official trophy description; Chapter 1 spot at Jason's house: PSNProfiles / community reports
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida — and start in Chapter 1. THE MISSABLE WARNING: one spot is at Jason's house during Chapter 1, and community reports say it can be left behind once the chapter ends, because the game has no mission replay. Do that spot before you finish Chapter 1, keep a separate manual save at the chapter transition, and then sweep the remaining spots as you explore each region. If you are past Chapter 1 without doing it, check whether the spot is still accessible in free roam before assuming a replay is needed.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Find Bret and hunt the unique animal he asks for. Hunting rewards patience over firepower: approach downwind, move slowly, and take the shot only when you are sure of it, since a spooked animal wastes the whole stalk. Bring a scoped rifle and track the animal's trail markers rather than wandering the woods at random.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full sets of collectible cards. Cards are scattered across Leonida — shops, hidden spots, mission rewards — so pick up every card you pass from the start instead of hunting them all at the end. A set only counts when it is complete, so trade your attention to the set with the fewest cards missing and use the collection menu to see exactly which cards are still out there.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK to scan 100 locations. This is a travelling trophy: scan everywhere you go, every time you arrive somewhere new, and the count climbs without a dedicated grind. In the endgame, drive a loop through the regions you visited least — the map's quiet corners are where the last twenty scans usually hide.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges from the game's challenge list. Challenges overlap heavily with the other trophies — stunts, races, robberies and exploration all feed them — so let them accumulate and only check the list when you are near the end. In the final stretch, pick the shortest unfinished challenges first; a handful of quick ones is worth more than one long grind.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose it. Get the heat in open country where you can run — rob a shop or cause a scene away from the city centre — then break line of sight, switch vehicles, and hide until the stars clear. Do it with a fast getaway car already parked nearby, and do not try it on foot in downtown Vice City.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without the wanted level dropping between them. Pick three shops close together on a quiet street, plan the route in advance, and keep moving — the trick is momentum, not speed. If the wanted level clears, the chain breaks and you start again, so choose a low-police area and go at a quiet hour in-game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Every new model you drive counts, so hop into anything unfamiliar — parked cars, traffic, boats and bikes all add to the tally. The fastest progress comes from variety: car meets, dealerships, docks and the airport parking lots each hold models you will not see in normal traffic. Check the vehicle list to find which classes you are missing.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one activation of Combat Focus. Set it up rather than hoping for it: find a group of enemies in the open, trigger Combat Focus when they are clustered, and work through them methodically instead of spraying. A mission with a wave of enemies is the natural place — let them gather, then activate and clear five before the effect ends.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from Vice City International Airport — in plain terms, steal a plane and take off without going through the front door. Get onto the airfield, take any aircraft, and get airborne; the trophy is about the departure itself, not where you fly to. Go at a quiet moment, keep your speed up on the runway, and do not stop to fight airport security.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Get into a Rhino tank and make it count — the trophy's own description is a wink at the vehicle's heat. Steal a Rhino from a military area, then use it in combat: the requirement is tied to fighting in the tank, so drive it into a confrontation rather than parking it somewhere safe. Expect heavy police attention the moment you roll out, so plan your route to open ground first.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Go in quiet: case the store first, move when staff are turned away, and take the goods without raising an alarm. If you are spotted, leave and try again — detection fails the attempt but the trophy can be retried as often as needed. A silenced approach and a clean exit beat a fast smash-and-grab here.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time. Banks are the heaviest robbery target in the game, so prepare each one like a small heist: armour, a getaway car parked close, and an escape route you have already driven. One vault per session keeps it manageable — five rushed attempts in a row is how you end up in cuffs with nothing to show for it.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks travel set routes, so watch one first: learn where it slows down, then hit it at a quiet stretch of road, grab the cash, and break away before backup arrives. A fast car waiting around the corner matters more than the robbery itself — the escape is the trophy.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore every region of Leonida: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga. The map fills in as you travel, so the simplest method is a deliberate road trip — drive the highways, take the back roads, and visit the towns the story never sent you to. Pair it with WAiNK scanning and vehicle discovery so one trip feeds three trophies at once.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida. Each gang controls its own turf, so this is a tour of the map's criminal corners: find one operation per gang, hit it, and move on. Keep a list of which gangs you have done — the trophy needs every gang, and it is easy to rob the same gang twice while thinking you are making progress.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, find a spot with a view of the water, and enjoy a cocktail there. It is a quiet moment of a trophy — no combat, no timer — so fold it into a trip to Vice City's beachfront and let it be the breather between harder objectives. Any beachside bar with an ocean view should do; sit, order, and let the scene play.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: METHOD UNCONFIRMED — the trophy's name and description are official, but no verified unlock method exists in public guides yet. The description points at a vehicle showroom: the leading community reading is to drive a car straight through a showroom's glass front and out the other side, in the style of the classic scene the trophy winks at. Try it in a showroom with a clear exit path, at speed, and if it does not pop, do not grind it — check back in this guide's updates, because the exact trigger is still being established by the community.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: METHOD UNCONFIRMED — the trophy's name and description are official, but no verified unlock method exists in public guides yet. The description points at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley: the leading community reading is to play a full game there and finish it with a proper follow-through — a strike or a completed game, rather than just walking in. Visit the alley, bowl a complete game, and if it does not pop, treat the method as still open and check community reports before retrying.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: METHOD UNCONFIRMED — the trophy's name and description are official, but no verified unlock method exists in public guides yet. The description is deliberately vague — 'a partnership with mass appeal'. The leading community reading is to raise both Jason's and Lucia's Strength attributes to maximum, training the pair together. If you are training stats anyway, max both characters' Strength and watch for the pop; if it does not come, the trigger is something else and the community is still working it out. Do not sink ten hours into one guess — check for a confirmed method first.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: METHOD UNCONFIRMED — the trophy's name and description are official, but no verified unlock method exists in public guides yet. The description points at choices that shape your Criminal Profile. The leading community reading is to perform 500 actions that affect the profile — the small decisions and crimes that add up across a playthrough. Play normally and let the count build; if you are deep into the endgame and it still has not popped, the trigger may be a specific choice rather than a count, and that is still unconfirmed.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: METHOD UNCONFIRMED — the trophy's name and description are official, but no verified unlock method exists in public guides yet. 'Second time's the charm' suggests a hidden second-chance event: something that goes wrong the first time and works the second. The honest advice is not to chase it blindly — keep playing, keep a manual save before unusual encounters, and if a strange event fails once, retry it immediately rather than moving on. The exact trigger is still unverified in public guides.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: METHOD UNCONFIRMED — the trophy's name and description are official, but no verified unlock method exists in public guides yet. 'What the hell just happened?' reads like a mysterious hidden encounter somewhere in Leonida — the kind of thing players stumble into while exploring, not something with a checklist. Explore the strange corners of the map (the Keys, the swamps, the mountains) and investigate anything out of place. Do not trust any single claimed location until more than one community source confirms it.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: METHOD UNCONFIRMED — the trophy's name and description are official, but no verified unlock method exists in public guides yet. The description is clearer than the others: knock people over with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a drive-by with a bat, not a gun. Try it on a slow drive through a crowded street, swinging as you pass; the precise conditions (how many, how fast, which weapon) are still under investigation, so treat any claimed recipe as a guess until the community confirms it.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies, so this trophy grows alongside the robbery trophies — launder the takings after every job instead of letting them pile up. Use your contacts regularly and the total climbs steadily; by the time the bank vaults are done, you should be most of the way there.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. This one takes care of itself if you buy gear as you play — weapons, armour, clothes, car upgrades — but if you have been frugal, the endgame is the time to spend: upgrade a favourite car fully, stock the best weapons, and buy the clothes you skipped. Check your total spend in the stats menu to see how far is left.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.source: Official trophy description; 8 garage properties: Exophase / PSNProfiles community reports
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties across Leonida. Garages are bought through the property listings, and they double as vehicle storage, so buy them as you can afford them rather than all at the end — the earlier you own them, the more use you get from them. Keep the money aside for the last one or two instead of spending everything on cars, and check the property menu for the ones you have not bought yet.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Whenever you find a vehicle worth keeping, register it through the app right away — ten registrations is quick once you make it a habit, and it pairs naturally with Whip It Good's vehicle discovery. Scooters, cars and bikes all count, so do not wait for rare finds; register the everyday vehicles too.
